title: T1595 Active Scanning
summary: Attackers probe your internet-facing IPs to see what is open and what versions are running.

title: T1566 Phishing
summary: Tricking someone into clicking a link, opening a file or typing a password. Now often by text or voice call, not just email.

title: T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application
summary: Using a bug in something exposed to the internet (web app, VPN, file transfer server) to get in.

title: T1133 External Remote Services
summary: Logging in through a VPN, Citrix or remote desktop portal that faces the internet, often with a stolen password.

title: T1078 Valid Accounts
summary: Using a real username and password (stolen, bought or guessed). Hard to spot because it looks like normal work.

title: T1110 Brute Force
summary: Guessing passwords over and over, or trying leaked passwords on many accounts (password spraying).

title: T1059 Command and Scripting Interpreter
summary: Running commands through a shell, PowerShell, Python and similar.

title: T1053 Scheduled Task/Job
summary: Setting up cron jobs or scheduled tasks so attacker code runs again later or after reboot.

title: T1547 Boot or Logon Autostart Execution
summary: Adding something that starts automatically at boot or login (startup items, systemd services, registry run keys).

title: T1136 Create Account
summary: Making a new account to keep access. On routers too.

title: T1098 Account Manipulation
summary: Changing an existing account (adding SSH keys, adding to admin groups) to keep or raise access.

title: T1003 OS Credential Dumping
summary: Pulling saved passwords or password hashes out of memory or system files.

title: T1021 Remote Services
summary: Using SSH, RDP or SMB with valid credentials to hop from one machine to the next.

title: T1046 Network Service Discovery
summary: Scanning inside the network to find other machines and open services.

title: T1071 Application Layer Protocol
summary: Hiding attacker commands inside normal-looking web, DNS or other traffic.

title: T1572 Protocol Tunneling
summary: Wrapping traffic inside another protocol (GRE, SSH, DNS) to sneak it past filters.

title: T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer
summary: Downloading attacker tools onto a hacked machine.

title: T1567 Exfiltration Over Web Service
summary: Sending stolen data to cloud storage or file-sharing sites so it blends in.

title: T1486 Data Encrypted for Impact
summary: Ransomware: encrypting files so the owner can't use them.

title: T1490 Inhibit System Recovery
summary: Deleting or wiping backups and shadow copies so the victim can't restore.

title: T1685 Disable or Modify Tools
summary: Turning off antivirus, logging or security agents. New ID in ATT&CK v20 (it replaces the old T1562.001).

title: T1195 Supply Chain Compromise
summary: Breaking into a trusted vendor or open-source project so their software carries the attack.

title: Ukraine power grid attack (2015)
summary: Business IT and grid control networks need hard separation.

title: Equifax breach (2017)
summary: Patch internet-facing systems fast, especially when a fix is public.

title: SolarWinds Orion supply chain attack (SUNBURST) (2020)
summary: A trusted vendor update is not proof of safety if the vendor itself is hacked.

title: Colonial Pipeline ransomware (2021)
summary: One old account without MFA can take down critical infrastructure.

title: Log4Shell (Log4j) (2021)
summary: Keep a software bill of materials (SBOM): a list of what's inside your software.

title: Lapsus$ extortion attacks (2022)
summary: Text-message MFA is better than nothing but is weak. Use an authenticator app or a security key.

title: MOVEit Transfer mass data theft (Cl0p) (2023)
summary: File transfer servers hold sensitive data and face the internet: prime targets.

title: Cisco IOS XE web UI mass exploitation (2023)
summary: Turn off management web interfaces on devices that face the internet.

title: Microsoft Exchange Online intrusion (Storm-0558) (2023)
summary: Signing keys are crown jewels. Rotate them and protect them in hardware.

title: Volt Typhoon pre-positioning in U.S. critical infrastructure (2024)
summary: Normal admin tools used at strange times or from strange places are the signal. You need a baseline of normal.

title: Change Healthcare ransomware (2024)
summary: Same lesson as Colonial Pipeline, three years later: one internet-facing login without MFA.

title: XZ Utils backdoor (2024)
summary: Curiosity about small weird things saves the day. Investigate the odd slowdown.

title: CrowdStrike faulty update outage (not an attack) (2024)
summary: Availability is part of security (the A in the CIA triad).

title: Snowflake customer data theft (UNC5537) (2024)
summary: Cloud accounts need MFA just like VPNs.

title: Salt Typhoon and telecom router compromises (2025)
summary: Routers are computers, and attackers live on them for years.

title: CISA credentials leaked in a contractor's public GitHub repo (2026)
summary: Never put secrets (keys, passwords, tokens) in a repo, even a "temporary" one.

title: SafePay ransomware (2026)
summary: Edge devices and backup servers are top targets. Patch the KEV entries for them first.

title: Verizon DBIR 2026
summary: Vulnerability exploitation became the top initial access vector (31%); only 26% of KEV vulns fully remediated.

title: Mandiant M-Trends 2026
summary: Median dwell time 14 days; exploits top vector (32%); voice phishing second (11%).
